2610.18867v1.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-improving Coding Agents for Physical Intelligence
2610.18867v1.authors: Wenyi Li, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Chunyu Liu, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Zheng Jiang, Deyao Hong, Calvin Xiao, Kaisen Yang, Qinhuai Na
2610.18867v1.abstract: Bringing general-purpose agents into the physical world calls for an executable representation of physical intelligence. Compared with vision-language-action (VLA) models, which map observations and language instructions directly to actions, code makes control logic explicit and reusable. Code can serve not only as a policy representation but also as the workspace in which the agent solves a task. Rather than following a prescribed workflow of planning, execution, and verification, the agent can autonomously inspect the state, revise and execute code, and use feedback to choose the next step. The success of this SWE-style loop in digital environments motivates its extension to physical tasks. Yet physical execution remains prone to recurring failures. To retain and refine experience for later scenes, we introduce EmbodiedEvo, where a coding agent evolves reusable Skills and Lessons through feedback on a single Playground scene, then freezes the resulting harness for diverse new scenes. On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

2610.18840v1.title: Seeing Double: The Theory Defying Twin Flares of TDE 2022dbl
2610.18840v1.authors: Xinze Guo, Ryan Chornock, Raffaella Margutti, Yuhan Yao, Erica Hammerstein, Natalie LeBaron, S. Bradley Cenko, Matthew J. Graham, Dina Ibrahimzade, Itai Sfaradi, Jean Somalwar, Robert Stein, Eli Wiston, Joahan Castaneda Jaimes, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Russ R. Laher
2610.18840v1.abstract: Partial tidal disruption events, in which a star survives a close passage by a supermassive black hole and may be disrupted again on a subsequent encounter, provide a unique probe of supermassive black hole properties and accretion physics. We examine TDE 2022dbl, a partial tidal disruption event candidate that exhibits two separate UV/optical flares, using 11 new optical spectra, updated UV/optical photometry, and a Keck-II/ESI host-galaxy spectrum. We trace the evolution of the prominent blended N III + He II feature across both flares and find that the blend evolves from N III-dominated to He II-dominated emission, which may reflect changing ionization conditions and a declining efficiency of Bowen fluorescence. The two flares show similar thermal evolution and spectral features, supporting a partial-disruption scenario. The second flare exhibits a broader, plateau-like peak, a longer decline timescale, and less extreme line velocities than the first flare. We suggest that these differences arise from the interaction between debris from the second disruption and an accretion disk formed during the first flare. From the host-galaxy velocity dispersion, we infer a black hole mass of $\log_{10}(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.01\pm0.45$. No third flare has been detected at the expected recurrence epoch, leading us to propose a new interpretation in which a positive-energy kick during ballistic core reformation delays the return of the surviving remnant.

2610.18635v1.title: DTScribe: Generating Models for Digital Twin Reporting using Local Large Language Models
2610.18635v1.authors: Kérian Fiter, Angelica Portocarrero, Bentley Oakes
2610.18635v1.abstract: The development of a digital twin brings together many stakeholders and technical components. We have previously investigated the reporting of the conceptual architecture for these digital twins as an artifact for discussion. However, we find that the activity of modeling the digital twin for visualization and consensus-building can be quite tedious and time-consuming. In this article, we explore the automation of model generation using large language models, targeting the model required for digital twin reporting. Our approach is designed to ingest digital twin documents and output both the conceptual architecture visualization and a reporting page for that digital twin. We first extract from the input the key details aligning with our twenty-one-characteristic Digital Twin Description Framework described in previous work. Then, we generate a description model in the Ontological Modeling Language, representing the digital twin as a constellation of models, data, enablers, and services. We utilize refinement loops with large language models acting as judges and ontological reasoning to increase artifact quality as measured by our metrics. We investigate how architectural and parameter choices affect artifact quality, such as how refinement loops enable local large language models to produce sufficiently high-quality results comparable to larger models. We also detail insights and lessons learned useful for practitioners, such that they can integrate our techniques to accelerate their digital twin reporting or for other model generation tasks. These insights include the use of medium-sized local models (around 20 billion parameters), the avoidance of large language models as judges and clustering for characteristic extraction, and the recommendation of at least two reasoner loops for Ontological Modeling Language refinement.

2610.18628v1.title: The Energetic Particle Detector Instrument on ELFIN
2610.18628v1.authors: Colin Wilkins, Ryan Caron, Ethan Tsai, Chris Shaffer, Patrick Cruce, Maxwell Chung, Andrei Runov, Jiang Liu, Drew Turner, Yuri Shprits, Wen Li, Michael Lawson, Emmanuel Masongsong, Cindy Russell, Eric Grimes, Jiashu Wu, Matthew Allen, Jessica Artinger, Alex Flemming, Brayden Hesford, Laura Iglesias, James King, Austin Norris, Carter Pedersen, Daniel Thomlinson, Wynne Turner, Vassilis Angelopoulos
2610.18628v1.abstract: We present the design methodology, implementation, and data products of the Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) instrument on-board the Electron Losses and Fields Investigation (ELFIN) dual SmallSat mission. ELFIN was designed to study the time-evolution of energetic particle distributions in Earth's magnetosphere, having operated in polar Low Earth Orbit (LEO) from 2018 to 2022. Each satellite's instrument payload contained a pair of detector heads to sense differential-directional fluxes of 50 keV to $\sim$5 MeV electrons (EPDE), and 50 keV to $\sim$2 MeV atomic ions (EPDI), with an energy resolution better than 50% ($ΔE/E<0.5$). The satellites were spinning with a nominal period of 2.8 s in a plane containing Earth's background magnetic field, with particle counting intervals subdivided into 16 consecutive spin sectors. Each EPD was paired with a three-axis Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) sampled at 80 Hz for local pitch-angle determination. Each detector head operated on the principle of pulse-height analysis (PHA) in solid state media, collimated by a rectangular 22.5$^\circ$ field of view and entrance aperture. The EPDE contained a stack of 6 silicon detectors (0.7 cm total thickness) with 0.15 cm$^2$ str geometric factor, with ion contamination mitigated by an aperture foil and digital coincidence logic. The EPDI contained a stack of 2 silicon detectors (0.1 cm total thickness) with 0.03 cm$^2$ str geometric factor, with electron contamination mitigated by a magnetic broom stage and digital anti-coincidence logic. The total assembled mass, volume, and power required for the EPD detector heads and circuit boards were 939 g, 10$\times$9.8$\times$8.4 cm$^3$, and 2.3 W, respectively. We describe each EPD design element alongside instrument data products and processing.

2610.18564v1.title: Observation Quality in DSM-Assisted Aerial Localization: A Benchmark and Base-Anchored Uncertainty Calibration
2610.18564v1.authors: Pengyu Yin, Junxiang Tan, Jie Pan, Mengqi Fu, Kun Cheng, Yifan Liu
2610.18564v1.abstract: Aerial map matching provides position observations for navigation, but a position error alone does not determine how an observation should be weighted. We define five benchmark tasks: position availability and agreement, grouped error structure, predictive uncertainty, controlled updates, and temporal accumulation. A case study in digital-surface-model-assisted localization evaluates base-anchored uncertainty calibration within this framework. The method combines propagated image and map sensitivities with the second moment of a compact configuration subset relative to the reported position. The reported position remains unchanged, and scale is fitted using separate position references without local surface-height ground truth. Thirteen covariance models are evaluated on two held-out query sets from locations represented in the calibration data. Relative to a constant full-matrix baseline, the method reduces equal-location normalized position-update risk by 7.70% on 728 conditions and 5.46% on a separate 142 conditions under an independent prior, with all localization failures included. On the primary set, equal-location negative log likelihood improves by 2.571 nat. These results show improved reference-based weighting at seen locations. Exploratory base-quality and conditional-addition controls leave the incremental update benefit of configuration disagreement unresolved. Navigation benefit and real temporal accumulation remain untested.

2610.18510v1.title: Contactless gait-derived features as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents
2610.18510v1.authors: Shuai Liu, Xiang Li, Guangxin Dai, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Hanchi Liu, Jiahui Niu, Yujie Nie, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan
2610.18510v1.abstract: Timely assessment of depression severity in adolescents is essential for guiding clinical care, yet conventional evaluations rely on episodic clinical assessments and symptom rating scales. Contactless gait analysis offers a potentially scalable approach to capturing objective behavioral features associated with depression. Here, we introduce the Long-Distance 3D Adolescent Depression Gait Dataset (LD3D-ADG), comprising depth-sensor gait recordings from 119 adolescents at a single center, including 39 healthy controls, 41 with mild depression, and 39 with moderate-to-severe depression. We developed UMLPA-GCN, a graph convolutional network that models spatiotemporal gait dynamics across three anatomically defined skeletal partitions. In participant-independent five-fold cross-validation, UMLPA-GCN achieved 75.63% classification accuracy, a macro-F1 score of 75.52%, and a macro-area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.839 (95% confidence interval, 0.779--0.899). Class-specific recall was 87.18%, 63.41%, and 76.92% for healthy controls, mild depression, and moderate-to-severe depression, respectively. At the participant level, reduced arm swing, slower pelvic movement, restricted joint range of motion, and greater arm-swing asymmetry were identified as leading potential digital biomarkers contributing to depression severity assessment, associated with higher 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence for contactless digital depression severity stratification in adolescents. Further external and prospective validation is needed to establish their utility for longitudinal monitoring and timely clinical assessment.

2610.18507v1.title: The Last Mile of Coding Agents for Long-Document Tasks: An Empirical Study on Clinical Trial Protocol Digitization
2610.18507v1.authors: Jiacheng Lin, Geoffrey Low, Nishit Agarwal, Rahul Jain, Afrah Shafquat, Mandis Beigi, Jimeng Sun
2610.18507v1.abstract: Clinical trial protocols serve as the source of truth for study design, but are mostly written and used as unstructured PDF documents. Digitizing protocols turns static content into structured, machine-readable data that clinical software can analyze, validate, and execute. Coding agents, which select tools, execute code, and revise their approach as they work, are increasingly applied to such long-document tasks, yet it remains unclear how reliably they turn complete documents into accurate structured outputs. We study this question using protocol digitization as a testbed. We introduce TrialPD-Bench, an expert-annotated benchmark of 150 publicly available protocol PDFs spanning four task categories. Beyond final-answer performance, our evaluation measures evidence recall from agent traces, agent behavior, and cost. Across nine proprietary and open-weight models in five coding-agent harnesses, even the strongest agents do not fully solve protocol digitization. Our analysis further shows that agents usually locate the required evidence but fail in the last mile of transcribing and structuring it. We further develop TrialScribe, a domain-specific harness that equips coding agents with task skills and a verification loop. TrialScribe improves a locally served open-weight model by 6.2-59.4 points across eight metrics, enabling it to match or surpass proprietary models such as GPT-5.6-Sol.

2610.18494v1.title: Task-evoked eye movements as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults
2610.18494v1.authors: Youxiang Sun, Yujie Nie, Zhuoru Wu, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Xiang Li, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan
2610.18494v1.abstract: Objective digital measures of depression severity could complement conventional symptom assessments and facilitate more timely clinical evaluation. Here, we investigated whether task-evoked eye movements provide interpretable behavioral markers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 155 participants aged 14--20 years completed emotional-spatial free-viewing and memory-guided recall tasks and were stratified by 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. We examined 19 prespecified eye-movement features across six task-informed domains using covariate-adjusted ordinal-trend models. Greater depression severity was associated with lower gaze-allocation entropy (standardized $β=-0.599$), fewer inter-area switches ($β=-0.526$), longer first target-entry latency ($β=0.572$), and lower target dwell proportion ($β=-0.678$; all false-discovery-rate-adjusted $q<0.001$). Emotion-specific attentional-bias measures were not associated with severity, whereas associations involving fixation dispersion weakened after adjustment for anxiety symptoms. In a complementary machine-learning analysis incorporating 44 candidate eye-movement features and demographic covariates, a three-stage cascade classifier achieved the highest four-class stratification performance (accuracy, 0.665; macro-F1, 0.670; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.869), outperforming single-stage and two-stage approaches. Together, these findings identify altered visual exploration and memory-guided gaze control as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity, rather than generalized negative attentional bias. These results support further prospective evaluation of task-evoked eye tracking as a complementary approach for timely severity assessment and clinical decision support.

2610.18366v1.title: Understanding the "Why": Investigating the Design of Privacy Support Tools (PSTs) through the Lens of Psychological Needs
2610.18366v1.authors: Sara Hahn, Verena Zimmermann, Simon Althaus, Andreas Heinemann, Ephraim Zimmer, Alina Stöver, Nina Gerber
2610.18366v1.abstract: Privacy Support Tools (PSTs) help users control their digital data, but face low adoption due to resignation and overwhelm. While current regulations aim to enhance privacy control, users still struggle to manage their privacy. To address this, we explore how PSTs can be designed for long-term adoption by applying the theoretical lens of psychological needs, as their fulfillment motivates users to use a digital product. We conducted in-depth interviews with 15 users and identified Security, Autonomy, and Competence as key psychological needs. From our results, we derive implications and recommendations for the need-sensitive design of PSTs.

2610.18311v1.title: BALLAST: Physics-Aware Moving Target Defense for Industrial Control Systems Using a Digital Twin Safety Oracle
2610.18311v1.authors: Oscar Mogollon-Gutierrez, Mohammadhossein Homaei, Alberto Lopez-Trigo, Andres Caro, Mar Avila
2610.18311v1.abstract: Industrial Control Systems run on static network configurations, which leaves an attacker unlimited time to map the plant. Moving Target Defense answers this by shuffling addresses, but almost every published scheme never checks whether the reconfiguration will itself disturb the physical process it protects, so the defense can destabilise a control loop or trip an actuator. We present BALLAST, which places a learned Digital Twin between the security policy and the plant as a safety oracle. A physics-informed LSTM surrogate forecasts the physical effect of a candidate network change, a reinforcement learning agent trades security entropy against process stability, and a connection-draining handover lets in-flight Modbus transactions complete before the old mapping is withdrawn. An explicit shield rejects any action whose predicted trajectory would leave the safe operating envelope. On the SWaT water treatment testbed, Ballast cut the success rate of an adversary's reconnaissance sweep by 85 percent and recorded no safety violation across 50 runs, a 95 percent upper bound of 5.8 percent on the violation rate, against five violations and a tracking error 19 times larger for RL-MTD, the closest published analogue to our design. Measured against the strongest baseline on the physical metrics, a threshold-triggered scheme that itself records one violation rather than RL-MTD's five, Ballast still improves the tracking error by a factor of 2.5 and removes that remaining violation. The gain costs a small and deliberate concession in raw deterrence. Twin inference meets the 50 ms budget on a workstation core and an embedded GPU, and is projected to meet it on both edge CPUs when the three envelope stages are evaluated in a single batched call; the complete decision-to-enforcement path was measured only on the workstation.

2610.18804v1.title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
2610.18804v1.abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. Our 3D foundation model, anatomix, is used to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes, and we further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system won first place in the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at http://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.

2610.18771v1.title: The Federated Tumor Segmentation and Classification (FeTS++) Challenge
2610.18771v1.authors: Wenyi Tang, Carla Pitarch-Abaigar, Siddhesh Thakur, Verena Chung, Konstantinos Koukoutegos, Alexandros Karargyris, Holger R. Roth, Spyridon Bakas
2610.18771v1.abstract: International challenges have become the standard for developing and benchmarking biomedical image analysis methods using centralized multi-institutional data. Federated learning (FL) describes a paradigm-shift on multi-institutional collaborations, where models are trained across institutions while their data are always retained locally. The Federated Tumor Segmentation (FeTS) challenge, first held in 2021, was the first challenge dedicated to FL in medical imaging and editions in 2022 and 2024 pushed the frontiers of real-world method validation. FeTS++ 2027 returns after a two-year gap with a substantially larger and more diverse cohort, and with the two "pluses" that name the challenge: an official classification task alongside segmentation, and a move of the infrastructure to NVIDIA FLARE (NVFlare). Built on the clinically acquired, multi-institutional multi-parametric MRI data of the BraTS 2025 Lighthouse challenge, FeTS++ spans gliomas and meningiomas across patient cohorts from institutions in North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa, and focuses on ranking submitted methodological approaches according to their model utility and an efficiency-aware score. Task 1 asks participants to find the best strategy for aggregating knowledge from per-institution segmentation models, while Task 2 asks them to distinguish glioma from meningioma under the same federated protocol, in which the entity label is heavily confounded with the site of origin.

2610.18765v1.title: What Human-AI Interaction Leaves Behind: Residual Human States -- A Trajectory-Based Framework and Multi-Study Analysis
2610.18765v1.authors: David Herrera-Poyatos, Carlos Peláez-González, Cristina Zuheros, Francisco Herrera
2610.18765v1.abstract: Human-AI Interaction is commonly evaluated by what an artificial agent enables during use, yet interaction can also alter the human who acts next. We introduce Residual Human States, a trajectory-based framework for representing the potentially multidimensional human state carried forward after interaction with AI, relative to a relevant alternative trajectory. The framework distinguishes assisted output from human-state transition and derives four empirical propositions: multidimensionality, interaction-policy dependence, horizon dissociation, and temporal persistence. Its central claim is that assisted performance does not by itself determine the human state carried forward. We examine these propositions through four empirical cases with different inferential roles. Published medical-training evidence illustrates how one AI interaction history can be associated with both slightly higher observed accuracy on some later unaided cases and transmission of a systematic decision bias on others. A second diagnostic-learning study shows that later unaided behaviour differs across AI-support policies, while also revealing that aggregate accuracy cannot by itself distinguish improved discrimination from a shifted response criterion. In a classroom experiment, generative-AI tutoring substantially improved assisted practice performance without a corresponding detectable gain on a subsequent unaided exam. A longitudinal reanalysis of personalised AI dialogue further shows that residual contrasts can evolve across post-interaction horizons and that such change may arise from the comparison trajectory as well as from the focal intervention. Evaluating interactive AI systems therefore requires attention not only to contemporaneous performance, but also to which human states alternative interaction trajectories produce, relative to which counterfactuals, and how durably.

2610.18728v1.title: Direct correlation of intravoxel incoherent motion imaging based on implicit neural representations and histopathology in pediatric Wilms tumors: can it differentiate between subtypes?
2610.18728v1.authors: G. C. Arends, M. Fitski, J. Harbers, J. N. van der Beek, R. R. de Krijger, M. M. van den Heuvel-Eibrink, A. F. W. van der Steeg, F. F. J. Simonis, E. Versteeg, A. S. Littooij, C. M. W. Tax
2610.18728v1.abstract: Wilms tumor (WT) is a heterogeneous pediatric renal malignancy. Invasive procedures to establish histology prior to pre operative treatment are not recommended by the International Society of Pediatric (SIOP) Oncology Renal Tumor Study Group, yet different tissue components are associated with different responses to therapy (SIOP Umbrella protocol). Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may improve subtype differentiation before surgery as a noninvasive radiographic biomarker by capturing both diffusion and perfusion characteristics, as opposed to the conventionally used apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). The objective of this study is to evaluate the discriminative performance of IVIM MRI in differentiating WT subtypes. IVIM provides quantitative parameters that disentangle the diffusion coefficient (D), incoherent blood flow (pseudodiffusion Dstar) and perfusion fraction (f). This retrospective study included thirthy children with WT. Standardized 1.5T MRI with 10 b value diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) was performed. IVIM parameters were estimated using a selfsupervised implicit neural representations network and were correlated with histopathology via a patient specific 3D printed cutting guide. Statistical analyses included mixed models, receiver operating curve analysis, and logistic regression. Thirty lesions were MRI histopathology correlated on slice level. Significant subtype differences were observed for Dstar stromal versus epithelial (p = 0.024), regressive tumors (p = 0.031) and mixed WT tumors (p = 0.043). ADC showed no significant subtype differences. Direct MRI histopathology correlation enabled differentiation between stromal subtype and epithelial, mixed and regressive subtype on macroscopic slice level using Dstar.

2610.18682v1.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning in Oncology
2610.18682v1.authors: Scindhiya Laxmi, Vivek S. Yadav, Ameya D. Jagtap
2610.18682v1.abstract: Deep learning has enabled substantial advances in oncology, including cancer detection and diagnosis, medical image analysis, tumor characterization, treatment planning, response assessment, and outcome prediction. However, conventional data-driven models often require large annotated datasets, exhibit limited generalization across heterogeneous clinical settings, and lack explicit mechanisms for incorporating the physical, physiological, and biological principles underlying cancer development and treatment. Physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) integrates governing physical laws, mechanistic models, physiological constraints, and domain knowledge into deep learning frameworks, providing a principled approach for learning from sparse, noisy, and heterogeneous oncological data. This review presents a task-oriented synthesis of PIDL methods across oncology, encompassing neural networks, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, convolutional and vision architectures, neural operators, generative models, and hybrid physics-data-driven frameworks. Their applications are examined across cancer detection and diagnosis, image reconstruction and analysis, tumor characterization, quantitative imaging, tumor progression, treatment response, radiation therapy, treatment planning, and multimodal clinical modeling. Based on the synthesized methodological and application-level evidence, we develop task-optimized PIDL workflows that align the clinical task with appropriate data representations, physical constraints, model architectures, and validation strategies. We further analyze key challenges, including physical-model fidelity, computational scalability, uncertainty quantification, domain generalization, standardized benchmarking, and clinical validation.

2610.18672v1.title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation
2610.18672v1.authors: Ziyang Song, Lia Shen, Yixuan Li, Qincheng Lu, Weihao Li, Haoran Xu, He Zhu, Xinyu Wang, Yue Li
2610.18672v1.abstract: Biomedical language models (LMs) provide strong representations for clinical tasks, but they often fail to capture the hierarchical structure among medical concepts. This limitation is especially pronounced for rare and fine-grained clinical codes in long-tailed vocabularies, where hierarchy-agnostic LM representations become less informative as concept frequency decreases. We introduce Semantic Medical Identifier (SMI), a training-free framework for constructing ontology-grounded Semantic IDs and hierarchy-aware medical concept representations. For each diagnosis, procedure, or medication concept, SMI defines its Semantic ID as the coarse-to-fine path through an expert-defined medical ontology. SMI then aggregates frozen biomedical LM embeddings across the corresponding ontology levels to form hierarchy-aware medical concept representations that preserve coarse-to-fine clinical semantics. The base SMI uses uniform aggregation across ontology levels, while a level-weighted variant selects global level weights on validation data. Our theoretical analysis shows that SMI yields more informative medical concept representations than hierarchy-agnostic LM embeddings, particularly for rare and fine-grained clinical concepts. Experiments show that SMI captures meaningful hierarchical structure and improves clinical relation prediction. On MIMIC-IV, SMI improves mortality prediction, readmission prediction, drug recommendation, and rare drug prediction. On eICU, SMI yields more robust patient representations under cross-hospital distribution shift.

2610.18634v1.title: Geometric Calibration of Supervised Fine-Tuning
2610.18634v1.authors: Jianzhu Bao, Jia-Chen Gu, Qingyuan Liu, Haozhen Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng, Wenya Wang
2610.18634v1.abstract: Recent studies investigate the weight geometry through its spectral structure, which characterizes how the weights transform different input directions. Within this view, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is shown to induce dense updates that perturb the spectral geometry of pre-SFT weights along their principal directions, potentially disrupting the model's prior knowledge. 2610.18564v1.title: Observation Quality in DSM-Assisted Aerial Localization: A Benchmark and Base-Anchored Uncertainty Calibration
2610.18564v1.authors: Pengyu Yin, Junxiang Tan, Jie Pan, Mengqi Fu, Kun Cheng, Yifan Liu

2610.18494v1.authors: Youxiang Sun, Yujie Nie, Zhuoru Wu, Mengyuan Yu, Wenkong Wang, Xiang Li, Yumei Wang, Xin Ma, Lizhou Fan

2610.18391v1.title: HULK: An Efficient Algorithm for Enabling Fast Bulk Bitwise Operations on Homomorphically Encrypted Data

2610.18771v1.authors: Wenyi Tang, Carla Pitarch-Abaigar, Siddhesh Thakur, Verena Chung, Konstantinos Koukoutegos, Alexandros Karargyris, Holger R. Roth, Spyridon Bakas
2610.18771v1.abstract: International challenges have become the standard for developing and benchmarking biomedical image analysis methods using centralized multi-institutional data. Federated learning (FL) describes a paradigm-shift on multi-institutional collaborations, where models are trained across institutions while their data are always retained locally. Built on the clinically acquired, multi-institutional multi-parametric MRI data of the BraTS 2025 Lighthouse challenge, FeTS++ spans gliomas and meningiomas across patient cohorts from institutions in North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa, and focuses on ranking submitted methodological approaches according to their model utility and an efficiency-aware score. Task 1 asks participants to find the best strategy for aggregating knowledge from per-institution segmentation models, while Task 2 asks them to distinguish glioma from meningioma under the same federated protocol, in which the entity label is heavily confounded with the site of origin.

2610.18728v1.title: Direct correlation of intravoxel incoherent motion imaging based on implicit neural representations and histopathology in pediatric Wilms tumors: can it differentiate between subtypes?
2610.18728v1.authors: G. C. Arends, M. Fitski, J. Harbers, J. N. van der Beek, R. R. de Krijger, M. M. van den Heuvel-Eibrink, A. F. W. van der Steeg, F. F. J. Simonis, E. Versteeg, A. S. Littooij, C. M. W. Tax

Invasive procedures to establish histology prior to pre operative treatment are not recommended by the International Society of Pediatric (SIOP) Oncology Renal Tumor Study Group, yet different tissue components are associated with different responses to therapy (SIOP Umbrella protocol). Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may improve subtype differentiation before surgery as a noninvasive radiographic biomarker by capturing both diffusion and perfusion characteristics, as opposed to the conventionally used apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). The objective of this study is to evaluate the discriminative performance of IVIM MRI in differentiating WT subtypes. IVIM provides quantitative parameters that disentangle the diffusion coefficient (D), incoherent blood flow (pseudodiffusion Dstar) and perfusion fraction (f). This retrospective study included thirthy children with WT. Standardized 1.5T MRI with 10 b value diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) was performed. IVIM parameters were estimated using a selfsupervised implicit neural representations network and were correlated with histopathology via a patient specific 3D printed cutting guide. Statistical analyses included mixed models, receiver operating curve analysis, and logistic regression. Thirty lesions were MRI histopathology correlated on slice level. Significant subtype differences were observed for Dstar stromal versus epithelial (p = 0.024), regressive tumors (p = 0.031) and mixed WT tumors (p = 0.043). ADC showed no significant subtype differences. 2610.18672v1.authors: Ziyang Song, Lia Shen, Yixuan Li, Qincheng Lu, Weihao Li, Haoran Xu, He Zhu, Xinyu Wang, Yue Li
2610.18672v1.abstract: Biomedical language models (LMs) provide strong representations for clinical tasks, but they often fail to capture the hierarchical structure among medical concepts. This limitation is especially pronounced for rare and fine-grained clinical codes in long-tailed vocabularies, where hierarchy-agnostic LM representations become less informative as concept frequency decreases. We introduce Semantic Medical Identifier (SMI), a training-free framework for constructing ontology-grounded Semantic IDs and hierarchy-aware medical concept representations. For each diagnosis, procedure, or medication concept, SMI defines its Semantic ID as the coarse-to-fine path through an expert-defined medical ontology. SMI then aggregates frozen biomedical LM embeddings across the corresponding ontology levels to form hierarchy-aware medical concept representations that preserve coarse-to-fine clinical semantics. Our theoretical analysis shows that SMI yields more informative medical concept representations than hierarchy-agnostic LM embeddings, particularly for rare and fine-grained clinical concepts. Experiments show that SMI captures meaningful hierarchical structure and improves clinical relation prediction. On MIMIC-IV, SMI improves mortality prediction, readmission prediction, drug recommendation, and rare drug prediction. On eICU, SMI yields more robust patient representations under cross-hospital distribution shift.

2610.18664v1.title: PlanPath: Exploration-Guided Orchestration for Patient-Level Pathology Reasoning

2610.18664v1.abstract: A patient's pathology case spans tens of slides from distinct specimens and anatomical sites, each carrying non-redundant, site-specific evidence. Experimental results show that PlanPath outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.4% and 12.1% in overall accuracy on the two datasets and further improves existing slide-level agents when plugged into our framework. 2610.18581v1.title: More Goods Means More Commitment
2610.18581v1.abstract: A seller without commitment to future offers interacts with a buyer over time. In the next period, the seller may again offer any menu of the remaining goods. Neither buyer nor seller can commit to future behavior. 2610.18874v1.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
2610.18874v1.authors: Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara
2610.18874v1.abstract: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. 2610.18873v1.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
2610.18873v1.authors: Wenxuan Guo, Yingping Liang, Zhaoguo Wang, Ziyuan Li, Angyuan Ma, Zhenyu Wu, Chengkun Wang, Bingyao Yu, Ze Chen, Borui Zhang, Xiuwei Xu, Meng Zhang, Erjin Zhou, Jiwen Lu

Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5\% average success on RoboTwin~2.0 and 49.5\% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. 2610.18871v1.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
2610.18871v1.authors: Chih-Hai Su, Tsung-Wei Ke, Yu-Lun Liu
2610.18871v1.abstract: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. 2610.18869v1.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
2610.18869v1.authors: Mingxuan Yan, Litian Gong, Dihong Huang, Zhixu Li, Tianyu Zhang, Wenqian Zhang, Hefeifei Jiang, Peihao Li, Jian Zhang, Mengfei Zhao, Yikai Tang, Hai Zhai, Zehao Wang, Ruijian Liang, Yanjia Huang, Lin Shao, Changliu Liu, Kaiyu Hang, Zhiwen Fan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Jianfei Yang, Jiachen Li

2610.18868v1.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
2610.18868v1.authors: Wenbo Hu, Shraman Pramanick, Krishna Kumar Singh, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang, Yong Jae Lee

Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. 2610.18867v1.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-improving Coding Agents for Physical Intelligence
2610.18867v1.authors: Wenyi Li, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Chunyu Liu, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Zheng Jiang, Deyao Hong, Calvin Xiao, Kaisen Yang, Qinhuai Na

Code can serve not only as a policy representation but also as the workspace in which the agent solves a task. 2610.18865v1.title: PLAYGROUND: Progressive Layout Generation with Render-Grounded Planning
2610.18865v1.authors: Jaeho Lee, Junhwan Heo, Junghyun Park, WonJun Moon, Eunju Yang, Seungho Jang, Seongchan Kim, Seungryong Kim
2610.18865v1.abstract: Generating editable graphic designs requires arranging visual and textual elements into a coherent composition while preserving their content and editability. Although recent MLLM-based approaches employ iterative generation and visual refinement to reflect the real-world design workflows, their high-level plans are predetermined prior to execution, limiting their adaptability as the design evolves. To address this limitation, we propose PlayGround, a progressive layout generation framework that dynamically adapts to the current rendered canvas. PlayGround establishes a progressive design loop comprising a Progressive Planner, a Layout Generator, and a Visual Verifier, guided by a Structure-Aware Retriever. Given an initial set of unordered elements, the Structure-Aware Retriever initially infers a coarse layout structure to retrieve structurally similar reference designs. Subsequently, at each turn, the Progressive Planner examines the current rendered canvas alongside the remaining elements, forms the next functional group, and plans its composition. The Layout Generator then predicts editable layout attributes, while the Visual Verifier evaluates rendered candidates and provides feedback when refinement is necessary. To train the Progressive Planner with step-wise supervision, we construct a two-stage data generation pipeline that extracts functional groups and turn-level planning trajectories from completed designs. Experiments on Crello and LICA demonstrate the effectiveness of PlayGround over existing methods. Our code and weights will be publicly released.

2610.18864v1.title: Simulations of the Evolving Ozone Layer: Implications for the Early Earth, Exoplanets, and the Search For Life
2610.18864v1.abstract: Over 4 billion years, Earth's atmosphere has been transformed from a composition devoid of molecular oxygen (O$_2$) to one where O$_2$ is now 21% of our modern atmosphere by volume. With high quantities of O$_2$, an ozone (O$_3$) layer can form and partially shield the surface from biologically harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV). The evolution of the O$_3$ layer has previously been simulated under the modern Sun by independent groups with separate models. Here, we present simulations of Earth's atmosphere from four open-source one-dimensional (1D) photochemical models and a 3D chemistry-climate model, focussing on O$_3$. We find that 1D models introduce a bias for unobserved climate states and show how these biases may propagate to calculations of biological UV damage and surface habitability. We show that when applied to specific exoplanet atmospheres, these discrepancies can become more pronounced, propagating through to observational predictions for the next generation of telescopes, such as HWO and LIFE, that will search for habitable and inhabited exoplanets.

2610.18863v1.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
2610.18863v1.authors: Dennis Grinwald, Ankur Singha, Khaled Kahouli, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima
2610.18863v1.abstract: Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations. Ultimately, our data-free training approach achieves comparable performance to training on HMC reference data.

2610.18874v1.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
2610.18874v1.authors: Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Xinxin Liu, Jiawei Zhou, Yuzhang Shang, Emilio Ferrara
2610.18874v1.abstract: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. 2610.18873v1.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
2610.18873v1.authors: Wenxuan Guo, Yingping Liang, Zhaoguo Wang, Ziyuan Li, Angyuan Ma, Zhenyu Wu, Chengkun Wang, Bingyao Yu, Ze Chen, Borui Zhang, Xiuwei Xu, Meng Zhang, Erjin Zhou, Jiwen Lu
2610.18873v1.abstract: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce \textbf{LoopWAM}, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67\% to 43.33\%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5\% average success on RoboTwin~2.0 and 49.5\% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20\% to 55.56\%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. \href{https://loop-wam.github.io/}{\textcolor{orange}{Project Page}}

2610.18870v1.title: Dog-Breed Text-to-image Flow Matching from Pretraining to Fine-Tuning on 4 Consumer GPUs
2610.18870v1.authors: Reyhaneh Esmailizadeh, Xingjian Leng, Zhanhao Liang, Liang Zheng
2610.18870v1.abstract: We generally perceive that training text-to-image diffusion models requires heavy compute: it is true if we aim at a comprehensive frontier model. This understanding prevents people from training their own models when getting started in the field. We develop MiniDog, a framework that enables pretraining diffusion transformers in 55 minutes and fine-tuning in another 15 minutes on four 3090 GPUs. For data, we use 26k dog images from ImageNet and caption them for pretraining and use 2k images generated by FLUX.1-schnell for fine-tuning. We precompute the image and text features and cache them for efficiency. For architecture, we use E2E-INVAE for its semantic latent space, a small transformer with 22M parameters, a small Qwen model for text encoding, and in-context conditioning. For training, we use iREPA and an EUPE perception encoder for acceleration. For evaluation, our repository supports FID, HPSv2 score, PickScore, and various VAE reconstruction metrics.

2610.18871v1.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
2610.18871v1.authors: Chih-Hai Su, Tsung-Wei Ke, Yu-Lun Liu
2610.18871v1.abstract: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/

2610.18869v1.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
2610.18869v1.authors: Mingxuan Yan, Litian Gong, Dihong Huang, Zhixu Li, Tianyu Zhang, Wenqian Zhang, Hefeifei Jiang, Peihao Li, Jian Zhang, Mengfei Zhao, Yikai Tang, Hai Zhai, Zehao Wang, Ruijian Liang, Yanjia Huang, Lin Shao, Changliu Liu, Kaiyu Hang, Zhiwen Fan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Jianfei Yang, Jiachen Li
2610.18869v1.abstract: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Across three VLAs, we find that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning; conditioning and filtering favor episode and chunk labels, respectively, on average, with model-dependent reversals; and constant-tag fine-tuning improves mean success after conditioned pretraining with either tagged or untagged inference. Built on crowdsourced simulation demonstrations, it provides recorded object and contact states for recomputing quality labels on shared trajectories. Replayable trajectories support workspace-aligned rendering and user-defined real-world target tasks. In our real-world experiment, simulation pretraining raises success from 9.6\% to 31.7\%. Project page: https://axis-bench.github.io/.

2610.18868v1.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
2610.18868v1.authors: Wenbo Hu, Shraman Pramanick, Krishna Kumar Singh, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang, Yong Jae Lee
2610.18868v1.abstract: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). 2610.18867v1.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-improving Coding Agents for Physical Intelligence
2610.18867v1.authors: Wenyi Li, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Chunyu Liu, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Zheng Jiang, Deyao Hong, Calvin Xiao, Kaisen Yang, Qinhuai Na
2610.18867v1.abstract: Bringing general-purpose agents into the physical world calls for an executable representation of physical intelligence. 2610.18865v1.title: PLAYGROUND: Progressive Layout Generation with Render-Grounded Planning
2610.18865v1.authors: Jaeho Lee, Junhwan Heo, Junghyun Park, WonJun Moon, Eunju Yang, Seungho Jang, Seongchan Kim, Seungryong Kim
2610.18865v1.abstract: Generating editable graphic designs requires arranging visual and textual elements into a coherent composition while preserving their content and editability. To address this limitation, we propose PlayGround, a progressive layout generation framework that dynamically adapts to the current rendered canvas. PlayGround establishes a progressive design loop comprising a Progressive Planner, a Layout Generator, and a Visual Verifier, guided by a Structure-Aware Retriever. Given an initial set of unordered elements, the Structure-Aware Retriever initially infers a coarse layout structure to retrieve structurally similar reference designs. Subsequently, at each turn, the Progressive Planner examines the current rendered canvas alongside the remaining elements, forms the next functional group, and plans its composition. 2610.18864v1.title: Simulations of the Evolving Ozone Layer: Implications for the Early Earth, Exoplanets, and the Search For Life
2610.18864v1.abstract: Over 4 billion years, Earth's atmosphere has been transformed from a composition devoid of molecular oxygen (O$_2$) to one where O$_2$ is now 21% of our modern atmosphere by volume. With high quantities of O$_2$, an ozone (O$_3$) layer can form and partially shield the surface from biologically harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV). The evolution of the O$_3$ layer has previously been simulated under the modern Sun by independent groups with separate models. Here, we present simulations of Earth's atmosphere from four open-source one-dimensional (1D) photochemical models and a 3D chemistry-climate model, focussing on O$_3$. We find that the O$_3$ layer thickness exhibits a clear deviation between the 1D models and the 3D model due to several factors, including treatments of O$_2$ photolysis, chemical networks, H$_2$O microphysics and 3D transport. We find that 1D models introduce a bias for unobserved climate states and show how these biases may propagate to calculations of biological UV damage and surface habitability. We show that when applied to specific exoplanet atmospheres, these discrepancies can become more pronounced, propagating through to observational predictions for the next generation of telescopes, such as HWO and LIFE, that will search for habitable and inhabited exoplanets.

2610.18872v1.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
2610.18872v1.authors: Yunsong Zhou, Xuekun Jiang, Haiqi Shen, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi, Yujie Liu, Jingyuan Li, Haoran Yang, Jiafei Cao, Dongzhan Zhou, Dong Wang, Yao Mu, Chunhua Shen, Weinan Zhang
2610.18872v1.abstract: Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. Against tracker-fitted references, the method reduces body-point error by 71.9% relative to the strongest baseline; matched evaluations also show gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning alongside humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.

2610.18850v1.title: Collaborative Planning for UAV-UGV Teams under Operational Constraints via Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion
2610.18850v1.authors: Zihao Deng, Qianhuang Li, Maggie Wigness, John Rogers, Donghyun Kim, Hao Zhang
2610.18850v1.abstract: Collaborative planning under operational constraints is essential for heterogeneous robot teams in large-scale missions. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) provide rapid area coverage but are limited by onboard energy, while Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) can serve as mobile recharging stations yet are constrained by road-network traversability. Effective collaboration must enforce operational constraints during execution while enabling parallel, coordinated actions. Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) have shown promise through token unmasking but have two key limitations: entropy-guided scheduling assumes distributional alignment and reliance on differentiable constraints for diffusion-time optimization. We propose Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion (MEND), which formulates collaborative planning as a conditional masked generative process to generate context-aware action sequences for UAV-UGV teams. MEND introduces a neuro-symbolic diffusion paradigm that constrains conditional masked diffusion policies at execution by reweighting the learned action distribution with a logic-induced admissibility indicator, thereby enforcing compliance with operational constraints. MEND introduces an error-bounded inference scheduling at execution that constructs the unmasking schedule by selecting positions with minimal predictive entropy over the constraint-aware action distribution, enhancing collaborative planning optimality under operational constraints. Extensive experimental results in simulation, on real-world maps, and with physical robot teams demonstrate that MEND advances UAV-UGV collaborative planning under operational constraints.

2610.18835v1.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
2610.18835v1.authors: Kaiyuan Chen, Shuangyu Xie, Uksang Yoo, Xinyue Zhu, Cael Magner, Alvin Zhu, Daehwa Kim, Eric Heiden, Erwin Coumans, Miles Macklin, Spencer Huang, Ken Goldberg
2610.18835v1.abstract: It is difficult to accurately model the physics of the interaction between a robot and the objects it manipulates, including contact mechanics, coupled contact dynamics, deformations, stiffness and friction. We present RoboSimStudio (RSS), an interactive toolkit that makes choices of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, allowing both humans and coding agents to iteratively refine simulations based on observed physical behavior. We implement RSS with the open Newton physics simulation system and describe experiments with human-guided real2sim using (1) visual evaluation, (2) force-feedback and (3) agentic Real2Sim2Real. Code, video and additional information can be found on the project website.

2610.18831v1.title: AegisAsync: Symbolic Async-Event Simulation for Risks in Python Asynchronous Programs
2610.18831v1.abstract: Security and robustness risks in Python async programs depend on event order, object identity, and execution after exceptions or cancellation. Detecting these risks requires connecting related operations across function calls and tracking their effects along execution paths. We present AegisAsync, a bytecode-based analysis of Python async risks for CPython 3.10-3.14. Its Async Event Transition Graph combines bytecode control flow, resolved calls, async events, and symbolic object relations. Bounded path-local simulation tracks event order and object states and explores cancellation at await suspensions. Six detector plugins evaluate the resulting traces and states to produce candidates with supporting witnesses. On AsyncBench, our benchmark of 180 labeled risks, AegisAsync detects all labeled risks with zero false positives on each of the five versions. Across five path budgets on 2,500 PyPI package versions, source review confirms 457 of 910 AegisAsync candidate records (50.2%), representing 457 unique bugs; across three flake8-async samples, 70 of 2,187 review judgments are confirmed (3.2%). By submission, 166 PoCs reproduce AegisAsync findings, and we have reported 157 bugs to developers, of which 16 have been confirmed and fixed.

2610.18830v1.authors: Francesco Di Clemente, Prachi Garella, Johannes Jahan, Micheal Kahangirwe, Jamie M. Karthein, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler, Claudia Ratti, Mikhail Stephanov
2610.18830v1.abstract: Inferring the possible existence and location of a critical point on the QCD phase diagram through experimental observations requires equations of state that include both lattice QCD constraints and critical behavior. 2610.18827v1.authors: Hemant K. Mishra, Mark M. Wilde
2610.18827v1.abstract: Loss and noise limit the use of light to distribute entanglement, transmit quantum information, and establish secret keys. Gaussian states have a compact description in terms of means and covariance matrices, but their entanglement still requires global optimization. We develop a framework for computing Gaussian-restricted versions of the relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement. An integral representation reveals a convex geometry under matrix geometric means and reduces Gaussian Rains entanglement to relative entropy minimized over Gaussian states with positive partial transpose. We obtain unique optimal reference states and additivity for independent Gaussian input states. Our convex-majorization algorithm has an explicit geometric convergence rate, uniform in the faithful regularization parameter and valid for pure input states. Controlled numerical integration and approximate convex subproblem solutions give a bit-complexity bound that is polynomial in accuracy bits for each fixed rational input covariance matrix, with explicit dependence on covariance size. These calculations bound extractable entanglement and, through the relative entropy of entanglement, extractable secret key. Finally, we separate the Gaussian-restricted quantities from their unrestricted counterparts and give a photon-number truncation method with controlled error for computing the latter.

2610.18825v1.authors: J. Arturo Esquivel, Jorge A. Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo, Sergio Pablo-García, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Vianey Leos-Barajas
2610.18825v1.abstract: Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.

2610.18822v1.authors: Ziheng Wang, Yanming Shao, Ting Mao, Kaihan Chen, Yiqun Wang, Xuanye Wu, Yao Mu
2610.18822v1.abstract: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to robot teleoperation for collecting dexterous manipulation data.
